_doc: Task 66: the involvement director (scripts/systems/involve.gd), never shown. While the pawn is awake, free (not at work or away) and has nothing open, every game hour adds pressure_step to the chance that something in the town touches them; when one lands the pressure resets. Never while a prompt is open; at most max_open things open at once. Open = a prompt, a guest or a knock, a scene on its way, an interview or a check-in within soon_hours, an overdue bill, a debt you lent out in the last day, or a pull within settle_min. The pool: weight per kind, early = times that weight in the first early_days, connect = a bonus when it involves people the pawn knows (a ripple always does). Kinds: visit (someone they know, or the neighbour, comes round: the door flow), favour / ripple (DailyHook favour; ripple = a friend who was just in something), wallet (DailyHook), scene (a StreetScenes scene where the pawn is), party (the neighbour's party), background (the background's next moment, SoloOpening.beats), grudge (someone angry with the pawn finds them), thanks (someone the pawn helped), questions (police ask about something the pawn saw), problem (a StorytellerTilt on a home incident: only odds, so it does not count as landed). town = the town's own events (TownLife): per_day across town, hour_mult per hour, lots_per_try, keep (how many are remembered), ripple_friendship, gossip lines. Variety: cooldown_h per kind, and nobody in a pull is in another within person_gap_h. call = a friend rings to meet up somewhere open (a real meet-up). approach = someone on the same lot comes over to talk (a stranger, someone known, a friend): the most ordinary pull, always real. neighbourly = someone who lives nearby knocks for an ordinary reason (no friendship needed), at home in the day. town.everyday = the ordinary friction and fun without a thread: two townies who already dislike each other have a row, a townie has a friend round (everyday_weight among the causes, everyday_tries samples). gossip_own = the line when the teller was in it themselves ({o} = the other person).

grudge_out: {n} blocks your way. "You've got some nerve, showing your face."
grudge_door: {n} is on the step, and doesn't look friendly.
grudge_sorry: "Fine." {n} looks at you a long moment, then lets it go.
grudge_stand: Neither of you backs down. {n} storms off. This isn't over.
thanks: {n} finds you. "I never thanked you properly. Let me buy you a coffee?"
thanks_yes: Coffee with {n}. You talk for a while; it's easy.
questions: A police officer finds you. "You were there when {a} was involved in that business. What did you see?"
questions_tell: You tell them what you saw. The officer writes it down.
questions_quiet: "Didn't see a thing." The officer doesn't look convinced.
call: {n} rings. "Fancy meeting at {place} in a bit?"
Your phone buzzes: {n}. "I'm heading to {place}. Come?"
approach_friend: {n} spots you and comes straight over. "There you are!"
approach_known: {n} wanders over. "How's it going? Haven't seen you around."
approach_stranger: {n} catches your eye and comes over. "You're new round here, aren't you?"
{n} sits down nearby. "Mind if I join you? Everyone else here is so serious."
neighbourly: "Sorry to bother you. I'm {n}, from round the corner. You wouldn't have a bit of milk, would you?"
"Hi, I'm {n}, down the road. A parcel of yours came to mine by mistake."
"Hello! {n}, just over the way. Have you seen a ginger cat? He's not come home."

row: Did you hear? {a} and {b} had a proper shouting match at {place}.
affair: You won't believe it. {c} caught {a} with {b}.
debt: {a}'s in trouble. Someone came round about money.
collapse: {a} collapsed at {place}. They took them to hospital.
alarm: Someone was messing with the cars at {place}. They're saying it was {a}.
gathering: {a} had people round last night. {b} was there.

row: I had it out with {o} at {place}. Don't ask.
gathering: I had a few people round last night. {o} came.
arrest: They pulled me in. It's all a mistake.
collapse: I took a funny turn the other day. They kept me in hospital.
debt: I'm in a bit of a hole with money, if I'm honest.
affair: Everything's a mess at home right now.
upset: I've not been doing great, to be honest.
